what: Invesco manages money: exchange traded funds including QQQ, mutual funds, and institutional mandates, charging a fee on the assets it manages.
customers: Individual investors through advisers and platforms, and pension funds and institutions directly.
money: fees on assets in ETFs, funds and mandates
moat: QQQ, the Nasdaq-100 ETF, is one of the most traded funds in the world and gives Invesco a position in passive investing that most active managers lack.
risks: A reported net loss of $316M, driven by write-downs
Active fund fees keep falling as money moves to cheap index products
The QQQ arrangement earns Invesco far less than its trading volume suggests
opportunities: 6.9 times free cash flow with $1.8B of free cash flow against a $12.2B market value
Analysts see about 27% upside, with 15 covering the stock
Revenue has recovered from $5.7B to $6.4B as ETF flows grew
watch: Net flows by asset class, and the average fee rate.
